answer_1.quote: We present a cost-effective framework for human-LLM collaborative stereotype data annotation and introduce EspanStereo, a multi-national stereotype examination dataset in Spanish created using this framework.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates stereotypical and anti-stereotypical sentences as part of the dataset construction, following the inter-sentence format of StereoSet.

answer_2.quote: In our evaluation metrics, stereotype scores (ss) closer to 50 indicate less stereotyping, while higher language modeling scores (lms) and idealized context association test scores (iCAT) indicate better performance.

answer_4.quote: We employ in-culture annotators to validate them. To ensure validation quality, validators must be born and raised in the target country and fluent in the target language.
answer_4.guideline: Validators are asked whether a specific stereotype is commonly observed in their countries, using a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 represents a stereotype that is never observed in the target culture, and 5 represents a pervasive stereotype.
